content.title: Market Movers: Metsera and Apple surge, Kenvue falters on Tylenol troubles
content.summary: Here are the stocks that made the most news today.

content.title: Kenvue Braces for Wave of New Lawsuits Over Tylenol’s Potential Link to Autism
content.summary: Kenvue  is preparing for an explosion of litigation over its popular pain reliever Tylenol after the Trump administration warned that the drug’s active ingredient is a potential cause of autism.  The finding by President  Trump’s  health officials, which Kenvue and some medical societies dispute, could provide ammunition to plaintiffs’ attorneys who are seeking to reverse losses in older lawsuits alleging the medicine caused the neurodevelopmental disorders.  Trump and Health Secretary  Robert F. Kennedy Jr.  said Monday that prenatal exposure to acetaminophen—the active ingredient of Tylenol and other medications—is a potential cause of autism.

content.title: Trump Warns Pregnant Women to Avoid Tylenol
content.summary: At a White House event, the president’s administration touted a little-known medicine as a treatment for autism symptoms.

content.title: Trump Links Autism to Use of Tylenol During Pregnancy. Kenvue Stock Hits Record Low.
content.summary: Tylenol maker Kenvue ‘strongly disagrees’ there is a causal link between acetaminophen use during pregnancy and autism.

content.title: Kenvue Stock Hits All-Time Low, Turns Higher After-Hours
content.summary: Shares of consumer healthcare firm Kevnue dropped to a record low during regular trading Monday, then made up some ground afterhours as President Trump warned that acetaminophen, the active ingredient in Kenvue's Tylenol, is a potential cause of autism.  Kenvue shares were down 7.5% Monday, putting them down about 23% since the company's IPO shortly before its subsequent spinoff from Johnson & Johnson in mid-2023.  Kenvue stock hit a record low and was the worst performer in the S&P 500 Monday.

content.title: Heard on the Street Recap: Even Tylenol Can’t Cool This AI Fever
content.summary: Nvidia makes a bullish bet on OpenAI.  The chip giant said it would invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI so that the company can build data centers using Nvidia systems to train and run its next generation of models.  Nvidia's shares rose 4%, adding nearly $170 billion to its market capitalization.
